predecessors.name: Hamdanid dynasty (emirates of Mosul and Aleppo)
predecessors.text: Diyar Mudar: Harran, Saruj and Edessa, from which Waththab ibn Sabiq broke away in 990

successors.name: Uqaylid dynasty
successors.text: Harran and Saruj, conquered by Muslim ibn Quraysh in 1081

successors.name: Great Seljuk Empire
successors.text: Harran, taken by the Uqaylids "backed by the Seljuqs"

ledger.x: 990: Waththab ibn Sabiq breaks from the Hamdanids and founds the Numayrid emirate at Harran.
ledger.cpn: Hamdanid dynasty (emirates of Mosul and Aleppo)
Hamdanid dynasty (emirates of Mosul and Aleppo)

ledger.x: 1081: the Uqaylids take Harran and Saruj.
1081: the Numayrid emirate ends with the loss of Harran.

wars.name: Numayrid-Kilab feud over Raqqa
wars.outcome: Shabib's death in 1039/40 'sparked a feud with the Banu Kilab over Raqqa'; Mani' lost Raqqa to Atiyya ibn Salih in 1062.

wars.name: Marwanid-Uqaylid attempt to retake Edessa
wars.outcome: Shabib joined a Marwanid-Uqaylid attempt to retake Edessa in 1036; the Byzantines kept it after peace in 1037.

wars.name: Uqaylid conquest of Harran (1081)
wars.outcome: Muslim ibn Quraysh, backed by the Seljuks, conquered Harran and Saruj.

certainty.note: Tribal emirate of Diyar Mudar defined by its towns (Harran, Saruj, Raqqa, Edessa); no frontiers on the page.
